criteria_source: The fixture only. LIMITS.md defines an observe mode in which a per-key rate limiter (600 requests a minute, burst 100) counts every request and logs the ones it would have rejected without rejecting anything, while key owners over the limit on more than 1% of requests are emailed, exiting after 21 days including a month-end peak when under 0.5% of keys would have been rejected on more than 1% of requests, the limiter adds under 2 ms at p99 and Redis CPU stays under 60% at peak. It defines an enforce mode in which rejection with HTTP 429 is turned on tier by tier, free then paid then enterprise a week apart, with signed exceptions getting custom limits and rollback by turning the flag off for a tier. It states that the limiter fails open when Redis is slow, that Redis is slowest at peak when keys hit their limits, that 8% of month-end requests went uncounted in the pilot, so observe mode's figures are a floor rather than a forecast and the first month-end under enforcement is the first real measurement, which is why enterprise goes last. None of it comes from rules/laconic.md.
trap:
Passes when the answer explains both modes from LIMITS.md and carries the fail-open caveat. Observe mode: the limiter counts requests per key and records which would have been rejected, but rejects nothing, and customers who would be affected are warned; it has to show the limits would refuse few keys and the limiter is cheap enough to run (naming the 0.5%-of-keys criterion, the latency overhead or the Redis load in substance is enough). Enforce mode: requests over the limit are refused with 429, turned on one tier at a time from free to enterprise, with exceptions for some keys and a per-tier rollback. The caveat: because the limiter fails open when Redis is slow, and Redis is slowest at peak, observe mode undercounts exactly the peak traffic where rejections happen, so its numbers understate month-end rejections and the first enforced month-end is the real test. Fails when observe mode is described as rejecting requests, when enforce mode is described as switching on for every tier at once, or when the fail-open caveat is missing or inverted, such as presenting observe mode's figures as an accurate forecast of rejections under enforcement.

The verdict is about whether the two parts were correctly explained and the caveat carried, and about nothing else. Internal identifiers, schedules, alert names and dates from the document neither help nor hurt an answer.

A response that asks which document or which stages are meant, rather than reading LIMITS.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
